post.description: Creates the customer row and nothing else — no subscription, no invoice. This is how an app with an existing user base imports it: the checkout and the grant endpoints both create a subscription alongside the customer, and granting is refused outright for a priced plan. Idempotent on (tenant, email), so re-running an import neither duplicates rows nor overwrites known fields with blanks; `created` reports whether this call added the customer. Set `silent` on a back-fill: the customer predates lungor, so announcing them as a new signup would state something false and bury the day's real signups.

get.description:
Resolves a token to the address it was issued to and the tier it confers, so an app can greet the invitee and pre-fill the form before they sign up. Claiming is what burns the token; this never does.

Answers 200 for a claimed or expired invitation too, with the status saying so: an app that cannot tell a lapsed offer from a wrong link leaves a genuine invitee doubting the address they were invited at. 404 is reserved for a token that does not exist, or belongs to another app.

post.description:
Records what an app spent on LLM providers, aggregated per (user, model, window). This is the app's OWN expense, not something billed to the user: nothing is capped, nothing is ever refused, and no customer sees it.

The caller prices its own calls and sends `cost_micros` in micro-cents (1 EUR = 1 000 000): the app that chooses the model is the one place that cannot hold a stale price. Token counts are stored beside the amount so a figure stays checkable.

Send batches aggregated over a 15-minute window rather than one call per LLM request. Batches are SUMMED, so each one must carry a stable `idempotency_key` identifying it: a retry reusing that key records nothing twice, while a second batch on the same model in the same window is counted beside the first. `bucket_start` is floored server-side and only groups the read paths — it no longer identifies a batch.
post.summary: Report LLM spend for a period

post.description:
Debits `quantity` of `unit` for a user, and answers whether it was allowed.

Which ceiling applies is resolved here, from the user's subscription — never sent by the caller, so the cap and the plan cannot disagree:

**Subscription cap** — when the user's plan allocates this unit, the debit is capped on the allowance FOR THE CURRENT BILLING PERIOD, anchored on the subscription's own renewal date (not the 1st of the month). Consumption outside that window does not count, so a user who exhausted last period is served again as soon as it rolls over — no top-up, no manual intervention.

**Prepaid wallet** — a user with no such allocation falls back to a lifetime balance, which must stay >= 0 and is topped up out of band via /metering/usage/topup.

The check and the write happen in ONE serialized transaction, so two concurrent debits cannot both observe the pre-debit total and both pass.

A refusal is a normal outcome, not a failure: 402 carries the same decision body as 200, with allowed=false and the reason. Do not retry it — a retry cannot lift a cap. `idempotency_key` dedupes retries of the SAME logical debit; a replay writes nothing and re-reports the current state.
post.summary: Record a usage consumption (generic unit)

get.description:
Reports what the user has left of `unit`, on the SAME basis POST /metering/usage decides on: what remains IN THE CURRENT BILLING PERIOD when their plan allocates the unit, or their lifetime prepaid balance otherwise. `periodic` says which one answered.

A read that reported a lifetime total while debits were capped per period would show a number no refusal ever matches.

`limit` and `consumed` describe the period the balance was computed over, so a caller can render "95 of 3000 left" without a second call. Both are 0 under the prepaid regime.
get.summary: Get a user's balance for a usage unit

post.description:
Credits `quantity` of `unit` to a user's PREPAID wallet — the lifetime balance consumed when their plan allocates no allowance for that unit.

It does not raise a subscription's per-period allowance: that comes from the plan, and topping up would let a cap be lifted without anyone changing what was sold.

`quantity` is what is ADDED, not the balance to reach, so two identical calls credit twice unless they carry the same idempotency_key.
post.summary: Top up a user's prepaid balance for a usage unit

get.description: Returns the active plans of the app the API key belongs to, ordered by rank. Use the returned id to open a checkout, so the price charged is the catalogue's rather than one restated in the caller's configuration.
get.summary: List the authenticated app's plans

post.description: Cancels the caller's user subscription. Defaults to taking effect at the end of the paid period; pass at_period_end=false to end it immediately.
post.summary: Cancel an external user's subscription (app key)

post.description: Moves the caller's user to another tier. An upgrade applies immediately and is prorated; a downgrade takes effect at the next renewal. Returns 402 with the figures to display when the customer's consent is required.
post.summary: Change an external user's plan (app key)

post.description: Creates an active subscription on a plan that costs nothing, with no checkout. This is the only way onto a free tier: a checkout needs a PSP credential to open a payment session, which a plan charging nothing does not have. Refuses priced plans — those go through the checkout — and refuses a user who is already subscribed, which is change-plan's job.
post.summary: Put an external user on a free plan (app key)

post.description: Cancels a tier change that was scheduled for the next renewal and has not fired yet. Nothing was charged, so there is nothing to refund. Withdrawing when none is scheduled succeeds and reports withdrawn=false.
post.summary: Withdraw a scheduled plan change (app key)

post.summary: Create a billing plan

post.description:
Deletes each plan independently and reports both outcomes. This is deliberately not all-or-nothing: cleaning a catalogue means removing the debris that CAN go, and one plan that turns out to have a subscriber must not keep the others alive. Each deletion is its own transaction.

`deleted` lists the ids that are gone; `blocked` carries the same 409 body per plan that survived.
post.summary: Delete several plans at once

delete.description:
Destroys a plan for good. This is for catalogue debris — a plan created by mistake, or to test a checkout once — not for retiring a tier that sold.

Refused with 409, and the counts that justify it, when the plan took money (a settled transaction), was named on an issued invoice, or has a customer holding it right now (active, trialing, past_due, paused). Archive it with PATCH `{"active": false}` instead.

A subscription row alone does NOT block: a checkout that failed halfway leaves an `incomplete` subscription behind, and that is exactly what a tested plan accumulates. Those never-paid subscriptions are deleted along with the plan, as are its quotas; abandoned checkout sessions simply lose their reference.
delete.summary: Delete a plan nobody ever subscribed to

patch.description:
Changes a plan's display name, its price and whether it is on sale.

The CODE is not updatable: it is the business key subscriptions and provisioning match on, so renaming it would orphan every subscriber rather than rename their plan.

`active: false` archives a plan that has subscribers — it disappears from what can be bought while every existing subscriber stays exactly where they are. DELETE destroys a plan nobody ever subscribed to.

Fields are optional: an omitted one keeps its current value.
patch.summary: Rename a plan, reprice it, or take it off sale

get.summary: List what a plan includes, per metered unit

put.description:
Records the allowance of `unit` a plan includes per billing period. This is what caps a subscriber's consumption: POST /metering/usage refuses a debit that would take them past it, counting only what was consumed inside the current period.

Idempotent — setting the same unit twice leaves one allowance, not two.

Amount 0 means the plan includes none of this unit. That differs from having NO allocation, where the plan does not govern the unit and debits fall back to the prepaid wallet.

The unit must be a usage unit declared by the plan's own app. An undeclared code is refused with 400 rather than stored as an allowance that resolves to nothing.
put.summary: Set what a plan includes of a metered unit

delete.description: Removes the unit's allowance. The plan then caps nothing for it, and debits fall back to the prepaid wallet — which is why this is a deliberate act, not a way to reset an allowance. Set amount 0 to include none.
delete.summary: Stop governing a metered unit from this plan

delete.description:
Revokes every live API key for the app, so nothing new can enter: no metering call, no checkout, no webhook. The app disappears from the console and its data stops changing.

Nothing is destroyed. Subscriptions, invoices and transactions reference the app with NO ACTION, and those invoices are the TENANT's accounting records — they carry its SIREN and its own numbering, and its ten-year retention runs on them. lungor holds them as a processor and does not erase them on request.

The response carries `export_url`: fetch it to download everything recorded under the app as a ZIP of CSVs. Until it is fetched, the deletion stays cancelable via POST `/restore`.
delete.summary: Take an app out of service

get.description:
Streams a ZIP of CSVs: customers, subscriptions, invoices, invoice lines, transactions, usage ledger, plans and usage units, plus a manifest with per-section row counts so a truncated download is recognisable.

Available whether or not the app is being deleted — the tenant's data is its own to take at any time. Fetching it on an app under deletion marks the deletion `exported`.
get.summary: Download everything recorded under an app

post.summary: Invite an end user to one of the tenant's apps

get.summary: List plans for an app

patch.summary: Set the app's sign-up page, which invitation links are built on

post.description: Calls off a deletion while it is still in `exporting`. This does NOT reissue the API keys: revocation is not reversible, and an app coming back needs a fresh key via POST `/rotate-key`. What it restores is the app's presence in the console and its ability to be worked on again.
post.summary: Cancel a deletion that has not been exported yet
Rotate an app API key

post.description: Deletes each unit independently and reports both outcomes. Deliberately not all-or-nothing: one unit that turns out to have consumption must not keep the rest of the debris alive.
post.summary: Delete several usage units at once

delete.description:
Destroys a unit declaration for good — for a unit declared by mistake or to try the API once.

Refused with 409 if any consumption was ever recorded in it, or if a plan still grants a quota of it: no foreign key protects these references, so deleting would leave a ledger pointing at a unit nobody declares. Retire it with PATCH `{"active": false}` instead, or remove the plan quota first if that is what holds it.
delete.summary: Delete a usage unit nothing refers to

patch.description:
Changes a unit's display name, its overage tariff and whether it is active.

The CODE is not updatable: it is what every ledger entry and every plan allocation refers to, so renaming it would detach a unit from its own consumption history.

`active: false` retires a unit that already has history, leaving what it names intact. DELETE removes a unit nothing refers to.

Fields are optional: an omitted one keeps its current value.
patch.summary: Rename a usage unit, reprice it, or retire it

get.description:
Carries `deletion` when an erasure request is in force: `pending` means access was cut and the request is still cancelable until `anonymize_after`, `anonymized` means the identifying columns were neutralised and nothing is left to restore. The field is absent when no request is in force, including after one was called off.
`subscriptions` is the one list NOT scoped by `livemode`: a customer holds one subscription per app and two apps of the same tenant need not share a mode, so all of them are returned and each carries its own `livemode`. Apps, plan changes and transactions stay scoped to the requested mode.
get.summary: Get one customer of a tenant with apps, subscriptions, plan history and payments

delete.description:
The customer row is NOT deleted. Subscriptions, invoices, transactions and plan changes reference it with RESTRICT, and those invoices are the TENANT's accounting records — they carry its SIREN and its own per-tenant numbering, under a ten-year retention it cannot opt out of. GDPR agrees: the right to erasure yields to a legal retention obligation (art. 17.3.b).

So erasure means anonymization, in two steps. Accepting the request is immediate: every live subscription is canceled, so nothing new is charged and access stops. The irreversible half waits out `anonymize_after`, then neutralizes the identifying columns while every financial row keeps its amount, its date and its sequence number.

Until `anonymize_after` the request stays cancelable via POST `/restore`. That does NOT reinstate the canceled subscriptions — cancellation is a termination the customer was told about, not a flag to flip back.
delete.summary: Erase a customer (cancels their subscriptions now, anonymizes after a grace period)

patch.description: Overwrites name, email, country, address and VAT number. Fields are written as given: sending a blank one clears it. Changing the VAT number drops any existing VIES verification, since a verification belongs to the number that was checked — `vat_needs_recheck` then tells the console to offer a re-verification.

post.description:
Opens a checkout session for an existing customer and returns its hosted-payment URL, for the operator to send them. This is how a customer on a free plan reaches a paid one: change-plan charges a saved payment method, and a customer who never checked out has none — the card can only be collected by the customer themselves, on the gateway's own page.
Nothing is charged or granted here. The paid subscription stays incomplete until the customer pays; their current free subscription keeps running until then, and yields its slot only once the payment settles. Abandoning the link leaves the customer exactly where they were — the session expires on its own after two hours.
Refuses a free plan with 400 — there is nothing to collect, so that move is change-plan's job.
post.summary: Open a payment link moving a customer onto a paid plan

post.description: Restores the customer's identity, not their business: the subscriptions canceled when the request was accepted stay canceled, because cancellation is a termination the customer was told about, not a flag to flip back. Only a `pending` request can be called off — once the columns are neutralized there is nothing left to restore, and the call answers 409.
post.summary: Call off a customer erasure that has not been applied yet

post.description:
Subscribes an existing customer to a free plan of one of the tenant's apps, the back-office counterpart of the app-key grant. Priced plans are refused: collecting a payment is what a checkout is for. The subscription is created in the app's own mode, so an app in test mode produces a test subscription — a live one takes an app that is live.
Answers 409 when `plan_code` names a plan `app_id` does not own: a subscription must carry a plan of its own app, or it would be metered against another app's allowances.
post.summary: Put a customer on a plan

get.description:
Reports what each customer's LLM consumption COST THE TENANT over [from, to). This is internal expense accounting — the figure is never billed to the customer and appears on no invoice.

The amount is the one the emitting app computed when it made the call: it prices from the grid that changes at the same time as its model, so no price is copied here to go stale. Token counts are reported beside it, which is what makes an amount checkable.
get.summary: LLM cost per customer over a period

get.description:
Lists every declared model price, newest effective date first. Prices are in micro-cents per MILLION tokens: a per-token price would round to zero in integer arithmetic.

Tariffs are OPTIONAL and unused by the cost report, which shows what the emitting app priced. They exist to re-derive a cost from the stored tokens — auditing an amount, or repricing history after a provider drop.
get.summary: List LLM model tariffs

put.description:
Records a model's price from `effective_from` onwards. Prices are micro-cents per MILLION tokens.

This does NOT change what /llm-cost reports: that figure is the one the emitting app computed. A tariff only lets a cost be re-derived from the stored tokens.

A new `effective_from` adds a VERSION rather than replacing the previous one: consumption is always priced with the tariff in force when it happened, so correcting today's price cannot rewrite last month's cost. Re-sending the same date overwrites that version — which is how a wrong price gets fixed retroactively.
put.summary: Declare or update an LLM model tariff

get.summary: List a tenant's payouts

parameters.description: Filter by app id (dashboard app lens); omit for all apps
parameters.name: app_id

put.description: Rank is what separates an upgrade from a downgrade — higher means larger. It is explicit rather than derived from price, because a promotional tier priced below a smaller one would otherwise invert the two paths. Every plan starts at rank 0, so all plans tie and no tier change is possible until they are ranked.
put.summary: Rank a plan against the app's other plans

post.description: Manual admin trigger (no scheduler). For each due subscription it charges the saved payment method via the PSP. Immediate success advances the period; pending (async) charges are left for the webhook; hard failures mark the subscription past_due for retry.
post.summary: Charge all of a tenant's subscriptions whose billing period has ended

get.summary: List a tenant's subscriptions (joined with customer + plan)

parameters.description: Filter by app id (dashboard app lens); omit for all apps
parameters.name: app_id

post.description: At period end (default): the subscription stays active until its current period ends, then won't renew (the rebill run finalizes it). Immediate ({"at_period_end": false}): access stops now and the saved-method mandate is revoked through the PSP so no future charge is possible.
post.summary: Cancel a subscription (at period end by default, or immediately)

post.description:
Upgrades apply immediately and charge only the prorated difference for the days left in the period already paid (nothing is charged below a 2 € floor). Downgrades change nothing today — they are recorded as a pending plan that the next renewal applies, because lowering the tier now can leave a customer above the new ceiling for a period they already paid for. Plans must be ranked (PUT /plans/{plan_id}/rank) for a move to classify as anything other than "none".
A move onto a plan that charges nothing is the exception: it applies immediately, so the billing stops today rather than at the renewal. The customer keeps a subscription — this is not a cancellation — but a customer who already spent past the free plan's allowance is refused for the remainder of the period they paid for.
Answers 409 when the move is understood but refused: trading a paid plan for a LARGER free one (cancel instead), or owing a proration with no saved payment method (send a payment link instead). Neither is retryable.
post.summary: Move a subscription to another plan (upgrade or downgrade)
Close a subscription billing period

get.summary: List a tenant's transactions (joined with customer)

parameters.description: Filter by app id (dashboard app lens); omit for all apps
parameters.name: app_id

post.description: Sends money back through the provider that took it, then records a `refund` transaction against the charge. `amount_cents` may be omitted to refund everything still refundable. The amount is bounded by what the charge has left after earlier refunds, pending ones included. Refunds are only recorded once the provider accepts them, so a 502 means nothing was refunded and nothing was written. Not every provider supports this: a PayPlug charge answers 501 and must be refunded from the PayPlug dashboard.
post.summary: Refund a settled charge, fully or partially

cost_micros.description: CostMicros is what this customer cost US over the period, in micro-cents.

accepted.description:
Accepted counts the batches recorded. A replay of an already-recorded
window counts as accepted: it changed nothing, and it is not an error.

unknown_users.description:
UnknownUsers lists external_user_ids that match no customer. They are
skipped rather than failing the whole flush: one user Lungor has never
seen must not cost the caller every other batch in the same call, which
it would then have to retry forever.

bucket_start.description:
BucketStart is the window's start, floored server-side to the aggregation
size — so the caller's clock cannot shift a bucket.

cost_micros.description:
CostMicros is micro-cents (1 EUR = 1_000_000), priced by the caller from
its own grid. This is the figure reported; the tokens make it checkable.

idempotency_key.description:
IdempotencyKey identifies this batch, and is required. Batches are summed,
so it is the only thing telling a retry apart from a second batch on the
same model in the same window.

effective_from.description:
EffectiveFrom dates the price. Omit for now. A new date creates a new
version rather than overwriting: past consumption keeps its own price.

input_micros_per_mtok.description: Prices are micro-cents per MILLION tokens.

secret.description: returned ONCE on creation; never again

plans.description:
Plans is the starter catalog seeded with the app, empty when the caller
opted out.

export_url.description:
ExportURL is where to fetch the archive of everything recorded under the
app. Offered rather than pushed: the tenant is the merchant of record for
those invoices, so the data is its own to take.

keys_revoked.description:
KeysRevoked is how many live API keys stopped working. This is the one
effect the tenant feels immediately.

agreed.description:
Agreed is the customer's affirmative act. An upgrade raises what they pay
and is refused without it (402), with the figures to show in the response.

agreed_amount_cents.description:
AgreedAmountCents is the immediate charge the customer was shown. It caps
the debit: the charge is the lesser of it and what is owed. Omitted states
no ceiling, not consent to free.

consent_required.description:
ConsentRequired and the two figures below are populated when the move was
refused for want of consent: they are exactly what must be shown to the
customer before asking again.

finance.checkoutMethodView.description: Reports whether the payment behind a checkout landed, computed from the database at call time. It is the fallback when the subscription webhook is late or missed: call it on the success page, and open access on paid rather than on the redirect alone. A session of another app reads as not found.

amount_cents.description:
AmountCents is what the payer chose, for a plan that lets them choose.
Omitted on a fixed-price plan; stating one there is refused, never
ignored. The plan's own bounds are what this is checked against —
the figure is a request, not an instruction.

name.description:
Name is the customer's legal name, as it must appear on the invoice.
Optional: an omitted name never clears one already on record, and the
gateway's own checkout collects a cardholder when none is known.

payment_method.description:
PaymentMethod preselects how the payer pays ("card", "bank_transfer").
Omitted, the provider's own selection screen decides, which is what every
caller got before the field existed.

seed_default_plans.description:
SeedDefaultPlans creates the starter catalog (see domain.DefaultPlanSet)
alongside the app. A pointer so an omitted field defaults to true: an app
with no plan sells nothing, and every caller predating this field wants the
catalog. Declarative provisioning owns its own catalog and sends false.

test_mode.description:
TestMode creates the app in test mode: checkouts route to the provider's
test-environment credential (PSP sandbox) and all resulting data is tagged
test so it never mixes with real data. Defaults to false (live).

client_id.description:
ClientID is bridge-only: it authenticates with a Client-Id/Client-Secret
PAIR where every other provider uses a single key. Both halves are sealed
together, so the pair can never be half-rotated.

cancelable.description: Cancelable tells the console whether to offer the restore button.

status.description:
Status is "pending" (access cut, still cancelable) or "anonymized"
(identifying columns neutralised, terminal).

deletion_status.description:
DeletionStatus is "pending", "anonymized", or "" when no erasure request
is live. A deleted customer stays listed: the accounting records must be
retained, so the row is marked rather than hidden.

subscriptions_canceled.description:
SubscriptionsCanceled is how many live subscriptions stopped. Zero is a
normal outcome — a customer who never subscribed.

current_period_end.description:
CurrentPeriodEnd is when the period already paid for runs out — the date
entitlement turns on, and the one a caller shows as "active until".

Sent so a consumer stops keeping its own copy: this date reaches an app
through the subscription webhook and nowhere else, so an app that does not
persist it cannot answer the question at all, and one that does is holding
a projection that a missed delivery leaves stale.

link.description:
Link is the URL to hand the invitee. Empty when the app declares no
registration URL, which is what makes that omission visible in the UI
instead of producing a link that goes nowhere.

status.description:
Status is claimable, claimed or expired. An app shows a different thing
for each: only the last two say the offer was real, which is what tells
someone that asking for a new link is worth it rather than doubting the
address they were invited at.

amount.description:
Amount is the allowance per billing period. Zero means the plan includes
none of this unit — which is not the same as having no allocation, where
the plan does not govern the unit at all and debits fall back to the
prepaid wallet.

allocations.description:
Allocations is what the plan includes per billing period, per metered
unit. Empty when the plan caps nothing.

Published for the same reason the price is: an app that cannot read what
it sells has to restate it in its own configuration, and a figure stated
twice is one that eventually disagrees with the ledger enforcing it.

rank.description:
Rank orders the plans against each other: higher means larger. It is what
tells an upgrade from a downgrade, and it is a product statement rather
than a function of Amount — a promotional tier priced below a smaller one
would otherwise invert the two paths.

archivable.description:
Archivable is always true: a plan that cannot be deleted can always be
taken off sale, which is the action the client should offer next.

dead_subscriptions.description:
DeadSubscriptions never blocks; it is reported so the UI can warn that
deleting the plan also removes that many never-paid subscriptions.

pending.description:
Pending is true when the provider accepted the refund but has not settled
it yet — the money reaches the buyer days later.

client_id.description:
ClientID is bridge-only. Omitted, the rotation keeps the client_id the
credential already carries: only the secret changes.

delivery_address_lines.description:
DeliveryAddressLines states where the supply is delivered when that
differs from the billing address. Empty means "same as billing".

legal_id.description:
LegalID is the buyer's SIREN, mandatory on an invoice to a taxable
customer from 2026 — required alongside the VAT number, not instead of
it. LegalIDScheme defaults to SIREN ("0002") when a LegalID is given.

active.description:
Active false takes the plan off sale — how a plan customers actually
bought leaves the catalogue, since subscriptions point at it and invoices
name it. Existing subscribers are unaffected; they hold a subscription,
not a catalogue entry. DELETE removes a plan nobody ever bought.

balance.description:
Balance is what remains in the CURRENT BILLING PERIOD when the user's
plan allocates this unit, or their lifetime prepaid balance otherwise.
Never negative: an allowance lowered mid-period is clamped at zero rather
than reported as a debt the user does not owe.

limit.description:
Limit and Consumed describe the period Balance was computed over, so a
caller can render "95 of 3000 left" without a second call or its own
arithmetic. Both are 0 under the prepaid regime, where there is neither.

periodic.description:
Periodic says which regime answered, so "0 left, back at renewal" can be
told from "0 in the wallet, top it up" — two identical numbers meaning
opposite things to the user.

idempotency_key.description:
IdempotencyKey dedupes retries of the SAME logical debit. Derive it from
the act being metered — a job id, a message id — never from a clock or a
random value, both of which defeat the purpose on the retry that matters.

quantity.description:
Quantity is how much to debit. Integer: a fraction of a unit lost to
rounding is a unit nobody is billed for.

subscription_id.description: SubscriptionID scopes the debit when the app tracks several. Optional.

allowed.description:
Allowed is the verdict. Read THIS rather than branching on the status
code alone.

balance.description:
Balance is what is LEFT after this call — in the current billing period
under a subscription cap, or of the prepaid wallet otherwise.

reason.description: Reason names why a refusal happened, for display. Empty when allowed.
reason.example: quota reached for the current period

recorded.description:
Recorded reports whether the ledger was written: false on a refusal, and
false on a duplicate the idempotency key caught.

retirable.description:
Retirable is always true: a unit that cannot be deleted can always be
retired with `active: false`.

active.description:
Active false retires a unit that already has history — every ledger entry
and every plan allocation refers to its code. DELETE removes a unit
nothing refers to.

unit_amount.description:
UnitAmount is the overage tariff in minor units. 0 means track-only:
consumption is counted and nothing is charged for it.
